analysis: The PR modifies only docs/architecture/inference.md. The patch excerpt shows scheduler geometry documentation changes near base 1087 and head 1087-1090, 1101-1148, and 2030-2047. The supplied units are base-side text for lines 1629-2248, so the changed head regions are not directly visible. I examined the visible base surroundings for security-relevant claims: native MiMo ownership and admission, media decode memory accounting, SSD prefix reuse, Flint tool and answer-stop constraints, the coordinator-serving channel, and invariants and failure modes. The changed text documents Gemma 4 wide prefill (2048/4096), a bidirectionalMediaPrefillChunkCeiling of 512, and solo-stripe behavior. These are runtime tuning parameters in EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift. They are documentation only here, with no code, auth, attestation, encryption, billing or wire-contract change in the supplied evidence. Nothing in the visible text weakens T-041 (prefix-cache SSD tier and TTL), T-008, T-010, T-028 or the TB-007 assumptions. The doc continues to state that memory admission, ownership-until-retirement and fail-closed behavior remain in force. Remaining questions for integration: whether the wider Gemma 4 prefill chunk (and thus larger transient prefill memory) is actually bounded by the process memory ledger and KV budget in code, and whether the 512 media ceiling really applies to bidirectional media attention. Both are code-side claims that this docs-only PR cannot verify; the head-side diff lines were not available in the supplied units. No concrete security regression was identified.
